description: We are a team of students from FPT high school, Vietnam. Fueled with passion for space exploration and technology. Interested in projects that combine AI, data, and real-time systems
summary: We developed DryDock, an interactive 3D planetary analog engine and equipment simulation platform that enables users to pinpoint specific locations on Earth sharing similar environmental conditions with Mars and the Moon. Inspired by maritime wave tanks used to test ship hulls before open-sea deployment, DryDock addresses the challenge by consolidating open satellite datasets from NASA, NOAA, USGS, and ISRIC—tracking elevation, terrain roughness, daytime and nighttime temperatures, humidity, soil acidity (pH), abrasion, and vegetation (NDVI)—into a unified coordinate grid. Using AI-driven data imputation to resolve sensor blind spots and a multidimensional similarity algorithm, DryDock cross-references terrestrial, Martian, and lunar terrains with real-time threshold filtering and instant coordinate warping. Furthermore, its integrated Equipment Simulation Chamber predicts thermal fatigue, terrain-induced vibration, regolith abrasion, and chemical corrosion on rovers, drills, and habitats. DryDock is important because it de-risks space exploration, empowering engineers to validate mission hardware in accurate Earth proving grounds prior to launch.
details:
1. Inspiration & Overview: What is DryDock? Before launching billion-dollar rovers, drills, or habitats into deep space, engineers need terrestrial proving grounds ("planetary analogs") that replicate harsh extraterrestrial environments. Inspired by maritime wave and wind test tanks—where ships and coastal structures are stress-tested in controlled basins before open-sea deployment—we built DryDock: an interactive 3D tri-celestial analog discovery engine and environmental simulation chamber for Earth, the Moon, and Mars.

2. How It Works & Technical Architecture

  • Data Consolidation & Python Preprocessing Pipeline: We aggregated multi-agency satellite and planetary datasets (NASA MODIS, MOLA, THEMIS, LRO Diviner, Moon Mineralogy Mapper M3, NASA PSG, NOAA ETOPO 2022, ESA Mars Express, and ISRIC SoilGrids). Using custom Python scripts, we processed raw GeoTIFF, HDF, and JP2 rasters, converting heterogeneous units (such as Kelvin and Thermal Inertia Units - TIU on Lunar Diviner maps) and resampling disparate resolutions into a standardized 100 km spatial resolution grid (~1° relative to Earth).
  • Multidimensional Similarity Engine: Rather than relying on superficial visual similarity, DryDock evaluates quantitative parameters across each grid node: Elevation, Terrain Roughness, Daytime & Nighttime Surface Temperature, Wind Speed, Dust, Humidity, Soil Acidity (pH), Surface Abrasion, Mineralogy, Radiation, and Vegetation (NDVI). It calculates a weighted percentage-based similarity score across Earth, the Moon, and Mars.
  • AI-Driven Data Imputation (Key Breakthrough): Planetary datasets often suffer from sensor blind spots, unit discrepancies, or missing coverage (N/A zones). DryDock utilizes AI interpolation trained on local topography, latitude, thermal inertia, and neighboring grid nodes to impute missing parameters and establish a complete target baseline.
  • Equipment Simulation Add-on: Once an analog site is identified, DryDock simulates how local environmental extremes—thermal cycling, terrain-induced vibration, dust accumulation, and abrasive regolith—impact mission hardware prior to deployment.

3. Product Highlights

  • Versatile Tri-Celestial Cross-Referencing: Start from any celestial body (Earth, Mars, or the Moon) and pinpoint corresponding analog sites on the other two with a 93%–99% match accuracy.
  • Real-Time Interactive 3D Globe: Features a dynamic "Match Threshold" slider (85%–90%), NDVI biological noise filtering (isolating 0.000 Barren terrain), and an Instant-Warp function (Click to warp to...) that transports users directly to target coordinates.
  • Multi-Source Data & AI Synergy: Combines empirical measurements from NASA, ESA, NOAA, and USGS with AI-driven gap-filling for comprehensive planetary coverage.

4. Scientific Factors Considered & Earth's Limits as an Analog

  • Beyond Visual Analogs: Two locations may look identical visually but differ drastically in mineralogy or thermal inertia. DryDock isolates specific physical dimensions so engineers can find specialized analogs (e.g., high-abrasion basaltic fields for rover wheel testing vs. extreme thermal-swing basins for habitat testing).
  • Accounting for Terrestrial Limitations: Good scientific analysis recognizes where terrestrial analogies break down. Earth has biological vegetation (which we filter out using MODIS NDVI) and cannot naturally replicate reduced gravity (1/6g on the Moon, 3/8g on Mars), the lunar vacuum, or deep-space radiation. DryDock explicitly flags these non-terrestrial parameters via NASA Planetary Spectrum Generator (PSG) radiation and atmospheric models so engineers can compensate for them in laboratory chambers.

5. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Data Processing & Backend Logic: Python (raster processing, unit conversion, 100 km grid resampling, and similarity scoring algorithms).
  • Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and 3D WebGL Globe rendering.
  • Design & Prototyping: Canva and Figma.
  • AI / Super Intelligence Disclosure: AI tools were utilized for coding assistance, debugging, data analysis/imputation modeling, and structuring documentation.

6. Intended Impact & Future Work (2027 Roadmap) DryDock accelerates pre-launch validation for space agencies and university researchers, cutting R&D costs and reducing mission failure risks.

  • March 2027: Upgrade the Research Tool Library inside the Simulation Chamber, allowing users to select specific rovers, geological drills, or habitat modules to view real-time wear-and-tear, wheel-slip, and load-bearing charts.
  • April 2027: Expand the Chemical-Mineralogical & Radiation Layer (integrating detailed Ilmenite, Iron Oxide, and Sulfate compositions) to simulate material corrosion and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU).
